brief: Equities fell to close the week as semis/AI names 'caught down' to NVDA, which the desk frames as the semis rubber band stretched too far. Macro toughened: VIX at 20, 10yr yields at 5.13% after a hot CPI print, USD breaking out, oil in the high-$90s. The move was rotational. NVDA shed $500bn of market cap while AMD and AVGO added ~$500bn+ combined. Flows show long-only supply in NVDA rotating into hyperscalers and other large-cap tech. LO and HF cohorts finished the week as moderate net sellers, and debate continues on the semis landscape amid Nvidia and election newsflow. Prime brokerage data show hedge funds net sold US equities for a second straight week (5 of 6), driven by single-stock shorts partly offset by short covers and macro buys. US ETF shorts fell 8.6%, the largest covering in 7 months, while 8 of 11 sectors were net sold, led by Info Tech, Financials, Healthcare and Staples. Financials' net selling was the largest in 8 months. L/S gross leverage rose to 209.1%, net leverage to 45.4%. Ahead: NVDA reports Tuesday under interim CEO Colette Kress, BABA Thursday, plus consumer earnings, Retail Sales and FOMC minutes. S&P implied move through 11/20 is 1.93%.
